To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the gains from trade, market liquidity, information precision, and the duration of the market all affect the incentives of market participants to acquire information.
the gains from trade, information quality, and market connectivity all affect the equilibrium amount of information percolated in the market.

(1) information is more readily acquired when the gains from trading are larger, (2) information is more easily obtained when the market is more liquid, (3) information is more likely to be acquired if agents vary more in terms of market connectivity, (4) information is more often acquired if agents are less informed to begin with, and (5) information is more frequently acquired if agents vary less in terms of their information quality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interdependence of market microstructure and information acquisition.
information acquisition in segmented markets, which are markets in which agents differ in terms of their preferences and information.
the interplay of information acquisition, market liquidity and the structure of market participants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the impact of information on market structure and vice versa is highly dependent on market parameters.
information acquisition is endogenously higher in larger, more liquid markets.
the market structure affects the equilibrium information acquisition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
information acquisition in segmented markets is endogenous, and it can be affected by the degree of segmentation, the gains from trade, and the duration of the market.
information acquisition is a function of the gains from trade, market liquidity and market duration.

market connectivity and the market’s duration are important determinants of the market’s efficiency, and that the gains from trade are crucial in determining the market’s equilibrium information level.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the information acquisition process is endogenously shaped by the structure of the market.
market liquidity is not only a source of information, but also of learning externalities.
information acquisition and learning externalities are endogenously determined by market structure.
